answer: The cheapest real defence: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because wander only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, walnut is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any nectar approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
